title: DDIL geospatial data logistics: versioned delta-sync and prioritized distribution of basemaps, 3D terrain and overlays across TAK Server federations and NGC2 edge nodes

scores.rationale: DDIL data continuity is a stated Army requirement (PM MC Operational Mission Command Suite notice, FACT/HIGH; UDRA RFI admits the mesh stops above tactical echelons, FACT/HIGH) and fielded-war evidence (CSIS on Ukraine Delta/Starlink dependence, 2024-12-11) shows shared pictures fail without link-tolerant sync; but the specific pain this gap monetizes (hand-loaded basemaps/3D terrain, manual overlay merge) remains HYPOTHESIS/LOW in the card with no unit SOP, AAR or IG finding captured. Real but unverified severity; confidence MEDIUM.

If the pain exists it recurs every pre-mission device load and every outage/reconnection cycle (INFERENCE from the card's current_workflow), and OWT's move to production (Vantor OTA up to $217M ceiling, BusinessWire 2026-02-25, FACT/HIGH) grows the 3D data volume that must reach the edge; frequency is plausible but rests on the same unverified workaround claim; confidence MEDIUM.

Score of 1 explained: the card itself states 'no dedicated budget line for geospatial delta-sync exists in public evidence' (Public evidence insufficient). NGC2 money flows through integrator-led OTAs (Anduril $99.6M prototype, army.mil 2025-07, FACT/HIGH) and is congressionally capped at 50% obligation pending a report (Federal News Network, 2026-02, FACT/MEDIUM); OWT is a data buy, not a logistics buy; the only funded analog (Immersive Wisdom $25M ceiling ordering contract, PR Newswire 2024-05) is a ceiling, not revenue. There is money adjacent to the problem but no identifiable owner or line for this product; confidence HIGH that no line is visible.

Nominal on-ramps exist (xTech, Army/AFWERX SBIR, DIU CSO/OT with no ownership test per E07-F22, TPC plugin listing) but five candidate requirement owners (PM MC/CPE C2IN, PEO STRI, AGC, NGC2 primes, TPC) share the problem and none owns it end to end, and the highest-value buyer (NGC2 divisions) is reachable only as a subcontract to Anduril/Lockheed team leads (E05, FACT/HIGH). Buyer fragmentation is the main drag; confidence MEDIUM.

Content-addressed chunking, delta encoding, CRDT overlay documents and priority scheduling under a bandwidth budget are mature techniques (Ditto's CRDT SDK and IPFS-style chunking exist commercially, FACT/MEDIUM); TAK Server public source and the ATAK-CIV SDK are open (GitHub TAK-Product-Center/Server and deptofdefense/AndroidTacticalAssaultKit-CIV, FACT/HIGH), so an unmodified-baseline plugin is architecturally possible. Hard parts are link telemetry and TAKX migration churn, not core science; confidence HIGH.

The card's PoC estimate ($150k-$300k, 2-3 engineers, 6 months, lab MANET, open data; analyst estimate) fits the founders' $250k for a lab-grade demonstration only; every step after (sponsor-gated TAK-GOV/MIL builds, exercise access, $1-2M credible military demo) requires non-dilutive or prime money the team cannot yet unlock. $250k buys evidence, not a company; confidence MEDIUM.

A measurable lab demo (bytes-to-converge vs native TAK data sync across scripted outages on 8-10 ATAK-CIV devices) is achievable in 3-6 months (INFERENCE, MEDIUM); a demo a military buyer would credit needs TAK-GOV/MIL builds and an exercise slot via a sponsor, which the card puts at 12-18 months. Middle of the range; confidence MEDIUM.

Everything needed for the MVP is open (OSM/OpenMapTiles, USGS 3DEP, Copernicus DEM, Cesium ion 3D Tiles, AGC's Releasable Basemap Tiles GeoPackage extension is itself publicly documented at docs.ogc.org/per/24-010.html, FACT/HIGH) plus synthetic overlays and scripted link profiles; OWT feeds and CUI exercise data are gated and needed only for the later military demo; confidence HIGH.

An EAR-only product (standard crypto under 5D002/License Exception ENC, E07-F32 FACT/MEDIUM) built on ATAK-CIV and open data is unrestricted, and no clearance is needed at MVP (S07 regulatory_access); but TAK-GOV/MIL builds and OWT data are distribution-controlled and a non-U.S.-person founder's access needs sponsor and export-control review (E07-F17/F18/F30, FACT/MEDIUM-HIGH), CUI handling triggers DFARS 7012/NIST 800-171 at the first DoD award (E07-F11, FACT/HIGH), and military-specific TAK plugins may raise USML Category XI questions requiring a commodity jurisdiction analysis by counsel. Medium burden; not a legal judgment; confidence MEDIUM.

Score of 5 explained: the entire MVP (two federated TAK Servers from public source, ATAK-CIV devices, open basemaps/3D tiles, WAN emulator) needs no government data, no sponsor and no clearance, and DHS/CBP and allied TAK users are an unclassified proving ground (S07 regulatory_access, FACT/HIGH; E07-F25 FACT/HIGH). Both founders can legally contribute to this stage; confidence HIGH.

Score of 1 explained (5 = least intense): the free government baseline already ships mission data sync, mission packages and federation (TAK Server, FACT/HIGH); CloudTAK's open-source /api/package/sync federation replication is under active development (skeptic-cited GitHub PR dfpc-coe/CloudTAK#1837, 2025, FACT/MEDIUM); a free community ATAK plugin (takwerx/map-depot) already downloads elevation and basemaps from inside ATAK (GitHub, retrieved 2026-09-25, FACT/MEDIUM); Ditto's Edge Sync plugin for ATAK is out of beta with ~$136M raised (company-reported, MEDIUM); AGC owns the Releasable Basemap Tiles program and OGC Basemap Tile Packages standard (ogc.org sprint page, FACT/HIGH); and Anduril leads the NGC2 common data layer baseline on Lattice Mesh (Breaking Defense 2026-06, FACT/HIGH). Absence of a single exact match is not opportunity when every neighbor is funded, free or government-owned; confidence HIGH.

TPC ships features slowly and the NGC2 primes have no incentive to serve non-NGC2 TAK federations or allies (INFERENCE, MEDIUM), which leaves a seam; but Ditto could extend a CRDT engine to tile manifests with modest effort (card's own incumbent_response), TPC can ship delta/priority sync as a point release with no market test, and AGC controls the tile-packaging standard. Incumbents are slow, not vulnerable; confidence MEDIUM.

TAK Server plugin API, federation protocol and the ATAK-CIV SDK are public and TPC-governed (FACT/HIGH), so a plugin that leaves the baseline unmodified is feasible; NGC2 data-layer APIs are controlled by Anduril and not public, OWT formats are PEO STRI-controlled, and the 2026 WinTAK sunset/TAKX migration churns the plugin model (Breaking Defense 2025-11, FACT/MEDIUM). Half the integrations are open, half are gated; confidence MEDIUM.

The core idea (CRDT plus content-addressed delta sync plus priority scheduling) is not patentable moat per the card's own defensibility section; the only durable assets would be TPC listing/accreditation, tuned scheduling heuristics from real link telemetry, and OWT/NGC2/coalition adapters, all of which the government or a prime can replicate or absorb. Thin, relationship-based moat; confidence MEDIUM.

Offline-first, bandwidth-budgeted tile/terrain/overlay distribution maps to wildfire and incident management, SAR, border/maritime agencies and field-ops in mining/energy (all TAK/ATAK-CIV adjacent, INFERENCE MEDIUM); Ditto shows the generic-sync version sells commercially, but the geospatial-specific market is fragmented and price-sensitive; confidence MEDIUM.

Allied/coalition TAK federations (NATO members, Australia under the AUKUS ITAR exemption E06-F27 FACT/HIGH, Bundeswehr D-LBO/TaWAN via the German founder), SOF, USMC and DHS sit outside the NGC2 prime data layer and Bold Quest 2025 showed network-limited coalition SA exchange (Systematic, 2025, FACT/MEDIUM); expansion into general edge data logistics is capped by the 'feature not product' problem and small allied plugin budgets; confidence MEDIUM.

TAK plugins listed on TAK.gov are typically distributed free to units, so revenue would have to come from enterprise/support/hosting contracts or an ordering vehicle; the Immersive Wisdom precedent ($25M ceiling over five years, ceiling not revenue) implies low-single-digit millions per year for an adjacent category. Recurring but small; confidence MEDIUM.

The strong engineer maps well onto the distributed-systems core and both founders can build the unclassified MVP; but the card lists a TAK-GOV/MIL-experienced plugin engineer and a geospatial data engineer as fatal-if-absent roles the team lacks, a 12Y/S6 advisor is needed to validate the very pain claim, the Indonesian founder cannot touch the sponsor-gated TAK-MIL/OWT half of the stack without licensing (E07-F18 FACT/MEDIUM), and a naive 50/50 cap table fails the SBIR >50% U.S.-person ownership test until the German founder's permanent residency is granted (E07-F3 FACT/HIGH; needs counsel). The German founder's allied channel is a genuine plus; confidence MEDIUM.

market.summary: No budget owner or line exists (card admits 'Public evidence insufficient'); NGC2 money is prime-gated and congressionally capped at 50% obligation; the free government/open-source TAK ecosystem (TAK Server Mission Sync, CloudTAK package sync) is already building federation data-package replication; five fragmented buyers mean nobody signs the check; the closest funded analog (Immersive Wisdom, $25M ceiling) implies a small, services-shaped market; and the SBIR/xTech funding path collides with the founders' ownership structure.

competition.summary: Three funded or government-owned tracks converge on the gap: Ditto's mission-ready Edge Sync plugin for ATAK (~$136M raised, ABMS IDIQ vehicle) on overlays; the Army Geospatial Center's Releasable Basemap Tiles program and OGC Basemap Tile Packages standard on basemaps; and Anduril's Lattice Mesh as NGC2 common data layer lead on division transport. The residual sliver (3D terrain delta-sync across non-NGC2 federations) is unverified and inside at least one incumbent's 6-12 month roadmap reach.

feasibility.summary: TAK Server already ships free delta mission-sync; Ditto already shipped a mission-ready ATAK sync plugin; the Army handed NGC2 division transport to Anduril in June 2026; and access/eligibility is structurally hostile to this team: TAK-GOV/MIL, OWT and CUI are gated for the non-U.S.-person founder, the SBIR ownership test likely fails on a naive cap table, AFWERX restricts foreign-national participation, and the $250k covers only the unclassified PoC with production dollars plausibly 2028-2030.

verdict_rationale: Kill as a standalone company. Three independent skeptics refute at strength 4 and I cannot show they are wrong with evidence; my own two checks this session reinforced them rather than rebutted them. Decisive reason: the PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE -> BUDGET -> CONTRACT VEHICLE chain breaks at REQUIREMENT OWNER and BUDGET. The user (12Y/S6/team leader) is identifiable, but no single office owns 'get the right terrain to the right device under a bandwidth budget' (five candidates share it), no budget line names it (the card's own 'Public evidence insufficient'), and the only concentrated money (NGC2) flows through integrator-led OTAs that Anduril now leads as common data layer baseline (Breaking Defense 2026-06, FACT/HIGH) and is capped at 50% obligation by the FY26 NDAA (Federal News Network 2026-02, FACT/MEDIUM). That is the major penalty the scoring rules require. Second, the capability is being built for free by the government-owned ecosystem: TAK Server mission sync and federation are baseline, CloudTAK is iterating package sync across federation peers in the open (skeptic-cited GitHub PR, 2025), a free community plugin (takwerx/map-depot, GitHub, retrieved 2026-09-25) already pulls elevation and basemaps into ATAK, and AGC's Releasable Basemap Tiles program has published its own GeoPackage packaging extension (OGC Engineering Report 24-010, FACT/HIGH) explicitly designed for offline tile caches and rapid coalition transfer. My RBT search found no delta-sync or bandwidth-prioritization semantics in the AGC/OGC material (FACT/MEDIUM: absence in what was retrieved, not proof of absence), so a technical seam does still exist, but it is a seam a government program office or TPC can close as a feature with no market test, and the pain that would justify a vendor filling it first (sneakernet basemap loading causing operational delay) is still HYPOTHESIS/LOW after two research passes. Third, the residual that no incumbent is positioned for (priority-aware 3D-terrain logistics across non-NGC2 and coalition TAK federations) is real but small, services-shaped, and structurally hard for this team: the sponsor-gated half of the stack is off-limits to the non-U.S.-person founder without licensing (E07-F18, FACT/MEDIUM), the SBIR path needs a cap-table restructure and the German founder's permanent residency (E07-F3, FACT/HIGH; counsel required), and the $250k buys only a lab demo. Market attractiveness 2.4/5 and founder fit 3.3/5; the founder-fit number is propped up by 'can start unclassified' and 'data is open', which are necessary but not sufficient. Confidence in the kill: MEDIUM, because the technical seam is genuine and a single verified AAR or PM MC solicitation naming bandwidth-prioritized geospatial distribution as a distinct requirement would move this to borderline.
narrower_version_if_borderline: Not recommended as a company, but recorded for completeness because all three skeptics converged on the same residual: an open, TPC-compatible TAK Server federation plugin and ATAK/TAKX client plugin that does bandwidth-budgeted, mission-area-prioritized delta distribution of 3D terrain (Cesium/OWT 3D Tiles) and AGC-standard Basemap Tile Packages across non-NGC2 TAK federations only (USSOCOM, USMC, DHS/CBP, NATO/Australian TAK adopters, Bundeswehr D-LBO/TaWAN), ceding overlay/object sync to Ditto and TAK Server, built solely on ATAK-CIV and public TAK Server source with open data and standard EAR crypto so the Indonesian founder stays clear of ITAR/deemed-export exposure, monetized through DHS/allied support-and-hosting contracts, xTechInternational or a DIU CSO/OT (no SBIR ownership test, E07-F22) rather than SBIR. Expect an Immersive Wisdom-scale outcome (single-digit millions per year) at best, and treat it as a 3-month, under-$30k demand validation (five 12Y/S6/SOF TAK admin interviews, one DHS or allied TAK unit willing to run a pilot, one TPC engineer confirming delta/priority sync is not on the Server roadmap) before committing the remaining capital.
most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders insisted on spending $250,000 here, the only defensible first build is a lab-measured, open-source-compatible sync engine: two federated TAK Servers from public source, 8-10 ATAK-CIV devices, a WAN emulator scripting 10-64 kbit/s links with outages, and a plugin that versions an AGC-standard Basemap Tile Package and a Cesium 3D Tiles terrain set into content-addressed chunk manifests and delivers only the missing chunks in mission-area-first priority order within a per-link bandwidth budget. They would show it to three audiences in this order: a TAK Server administrator or S6 in a SOF unit or DHS/CBP TAK deployment (the user who has lived through resync failures), a TAK Product Center engineer (the gatekeeper who decides whether this is a roadmap feature or a listed plugin), and a PEO STRI OWT lead (who wants OWT usable at the edge). The demonstration must prove a measured 5-10x reduction in bytes-to-converge and time-to-converge after outages versus native TAK mission packages and data sync, with mission-area terrain arriving first and a pre-mission 'what is stale on this device' report, running on an unmodified TAK Server baseline. The customer would care only if the pain is real: that a geospatial NCO can replace USB loading and terrain that is never refreshed with a policy like 'keep AO tiles fresh within 24 hours' over the radio link they actually have. The honest answer to 'why can't an incumbent trivially crush them' is that an incumbent can: TPC can ship delta/priority sync as a Server release, Ditto can extend its CRDT engine to tile manifests, and Anduril owns NGC2 transport; the founders' only protection is speed to a TPC-listed plugin that non-NGC2 units already run, plus tuned scheduling heuristics from real link telemetry, which is a head start rather than a moat. The milestone that would justify the next $2-5 million is not the lab number; it is a primary-source demand signal that does not exist today: a unit AAR or S6 statement that the plugin removed sneakernet terrain loading in a live exercise, a PM MC, USSOCOM or DHS solicitation or task order naming bandwidth-prioritized geospatial distribution as a distinct requirement, and a TPC engineer confirming in writing that this function is not on the Server roadmap. Because that signal was not found in two research passes and the incumbent structure makes it unlikely to be left open for a startup, this gap fails: the founders would be spending $250k to discover whether a feature is a product, with the odds and the funding structure both against them.
bear_case_summary: No budget line and no accountable requirement owner; NGC2 money is prime-gated, Anduril-led and congressionally capped; the free government/open-source TAK ecosystem (TAK Server sync, CloudTAK package sync, community map-depot plugin, AGC Releasable Basemap Tiles) is already building the surrounding capability; Ditto covers overlay sync with ~$136M and a mission-ready ATAK plugin; the core pain claim is still HYPOTHESIS/LOW; the residual market is Immersive Wisdom-scale; and the founders' ownership and export-control situation blocks SBIR and the sponsor-gated half of the stack.
bull_case_summary: DDIL data continuity is a stated Army requirement, the UDRA RFI admits the data mesh stops above tactical echelons, OWT going to production multiplies the 3D data that must reach edge devices, coalition exercises (Bold Quest 2025) show network-limited SA exchange, nobody has evidenced bandwidth-budgeted, priority-aware delta distribution of 3D terrain across TAK federations (my AGC/OGC RBT check found packaging only, no distribution semantics), the whole MVP is buildable unclassified on open data, and allied/SOF/DHS TAK users sit permanently outside the NGC2 prime data layer where the German founder has a warm channel.
